cases.title: The Field Hospital Trap
cases.presentation: Your treatment area has 8 reds. Two paramedics are attempting RSI on one red, another is placing a second IV on a stable yellow. Four ambulances wait empty at the loading zone.
cases.question: Best correction?
options: A: Transport yellows first since they're ready.
B: Send ambulances back to staging.
C: Load reds now with essential interventions only (airway positioning/adjuncts, bleeding control, decompression); do advanced procedures en route or at hospital.
cases.explanation: Idle ambulances + waiting reds = flow failure. Treat to the minimum that's safe for transport and move.
cases.clinicalPearl: Empty ambulances are a red flag in the treatment area.

cases.title: Three Hospitals, One Plan
cases.presentation: Subway derailment: 6 red, 10 yellow, 25 green. Hospitals: Central (Level I, 6 min — already receiving 15 walk-ins), East (community, 12 min, 10 free ED beds), Children's (15 min). 2 reds are children.
cases.question: Best distribution?
options: A: Greens first to clear the scene.
C: Hold all patients until hospitals call back.

D: Adult reds split between Central and the next trauma-capable hospital, pediatric reds toward Children's if stable enough for 15 min, yellows to East, greens by bus to the least-loaded facility — all via Med Comms and logged.
cases.explanation: Match capability, respect capacity, and protect the trauma center for those who need it. Central is already flooded by self-presenters.
cases.clinicalPearl: Ask hospitals for capacity by color: 'How many red, yellow, green can you take?'
